Stop 1 · Sep 19–22
Madrid
3 Nights A Bright Apartment in Sol
The capital first — art, energy, and the heart of Spain
1Day
Arrival in Madrid
Saturday, September 19, 2026
Morning
Land at Madrid Barajas at 9:05 AM after the overnight from Dallas. Take a taxi or Metro Line 8 (~40 minutes) into central Madrid — no car needed for your first three days in the city. Check in to the Sol apartment from 3:00 PM and rest up.
Afternoon
Check in to A Bright Apartment in Sol on Calle de Espoz y Mina — you’re steps from Puerta del Sol, the literal center of Spain. Freshen up after the overnight flight. A slow walk around the neighborhood is the perfect re-entry to civilization.
Evening
Easy first night. Plaza Mayor and Puerta del Sol are on your doorstep. Grab a table at a classic tapas bar — jamón ibérico, patatas bravas, a glass of Rioja. Early bed after a long travel day.
🏠
A Bright Apartment in Sol

Confirmation: HMZ2245WTT · +34 658 75 62 27
2Day
The Prado & Retiro Park
Sunday, September 20, 2026
Morning
Museo del Prado — timed entry booked for 10:15 AM. One of the great art museums of the world. Prioritize Velázquez’s Las Menínas, Goya’s Black Paintings, and El Greco’s elongated saints. Allow 2–3 hours minimum. Go straight to the access door — no need to queue at the ticket office.
🎨
Museo Nacional del Prado — Timed Entry
Sunday, September 20, 2026 · 10:15 AM · 4 General tickets · €60.00 total · Go directly to access door · No backpacks, no photos
Localizador: M393957F · Identifiers: M393957F-1 through M393957F-4 · museodelprado.es
Afternoon
Retiro Park — rent a rowboat on the lake, visit the stunning iron-and-glass Crystal Palace, and decompress in Madrid’s great urban lung. A perfect September afternoon.
Evening
Dinner in La Latina or Malasaña — Madrid’s liveliest neighborhoods for food and bars. The city doesn’t eat until 9 PM; lean into the rhythm.
3Day
Royal Palace & Reina Sofía
Monday, September 21, 2026
Morning
Palacio Real — the official royal residence, staggeringly opulent with 3,418 rooms, Tiepolo frescoes, and the royal armory. Book ahead to skip the queue. The adjacent Sabatini Gardens are free and lovely for a morning stroll.
Afternoon
Museo Reina Sofía — Picasso’s Guernica in person is a genuinely moving experience. The museum also holds the Spanish surrealists: Dalí, Miró, and their contemporaries. Book timed entry.
Evening
Pack tonight for tomorrow’s early departure south. Farewell Madrid dinner — try a classic asador for cochinillo (roast suckling pig) or a rooftop bar for a last look at the city skyline.
🚗
Travel · Tuesday, September 22, 2026 · ~4.5 hrs with stop
Madrid → Consuegra → Córdoba
Pick up Hertz rental car (Skoda Karoq or similar) at Atocha Railway Station at 8:00 AM · Head south via A-4 · Detour to Consuegra windmills (~1.5 hrs from Madrid) · Continue south through La Mancha · Arrive Córdoba early afternoon · Check in from 3:00 PM
Stop 2 · Sep 22–24
Córdoba
2 Nights Olivia Suites Apartments 1
Where three faiths built one of the world’s great cities
4Day
Arrival in Córdoba
Tuesday, September 22, 2026
Morning / Drive
Pick up the Hertz at Atocha at 8:00 AM and head south on the A-4. About 90 minutes out, detour to Consuegra — 12 iconic white windmills strung along a hilltop ridge above a medieval castle, right in the heart of La Mancha. These are the windmills of Don Quixote, and in person they're every bit as dramatic as you'd imagine. The ridge walk takes 20–30 minutes and the views across the Castilian plain are spectacular — bring your camera, Mark. Then back on the A-4 south as the landscape shifts into Andalucía.
Afternoon
Check in to Olivia Suites Apartments 1 (available from 3:00 PM) on Calle Romero, right in the heart of the old city. Freshen up and take a slow first wander through the Judeía streets.
Evening
Easy first night in Córdoba. Find a terrace bar near the Mezquita, order cold Cruzcampo and a plate of salmorejo, and let the city introduce itself at its own pace.
🏠

Confirmation: HMK9XSC548 · Host: PyR Apartments · +34 640 84 87 94
5Day
The Mezquita & Jewish Quarter
Wednesday, September 23, 2026
Morning
Mezquita-Cathedral — book the earliest entry slot. The forest of 856 red-and-white striped arches is one of the most breathtaking interiors in the world. A mosque for 300 years, then a cathedral built inside it. Allow 2 hours minimum. The bell tower view is worth the climb.
Midday
Cross the Puente Romano (Roman Bridge) for views back toward the Mezquita. Lunch in the Judeía (Jewish Quarter) — winding whitewashed streets, flower-filled patios, and hidden courtyards. Find the small Sinagoga nearby, one of only three surviving medieval synagogues in Spain.
Afternoon
Explore the Alcázar de los Reyes Cristianos — the royal fortress where Ferdinand and Isabella received Columbus. Beautiful terraced gardens. In late September you’ll have soft afternoon light on the reflecting pools.
Evening
Córdoba’s tapas culture is underrated. Bar hop around Plaza de la Corredera — the city’s grand porticoed square — for local wine, jamón, and flamequín (Córdoba’s own breaded pork roll).
6Day
Medina Azahara & Patios
Thursday, September 24, 2026 — Checkout by Noon
Morning
Medina Azahara — drive 8km west to this astonishing ruined 10th-century Moorish palace city, built by Caliph Abd al-Rahman III. A UNESCO site since 2018, it covers 112 hectares on a hillside. The museum puts the excavated mosaics and carved stonework in context. Book tickets in advance — limited daily entries.
Afternoon
Back in the city, explore the patio culture Córdoba is famous for — private courtyards blazing with flowers and tilework. Many are open year-round; even outside the May festival, the old city streets reward slow walking and peering through iron gates.
Evening
Farewell Córdoba dinner. Try Taberna Salinas (founded 1879) or similar old-school taberna for rabo de toro (oxtail stew) and Montilla-Moriles wine — the local answer to sherry.
🚗
Travel · Thursday, September 24, 2026 · ~1.5 hrs
Córdoba → Seville
Checkout by 12:00 PM · Easy drive southwest via A-4 · Check in Seville from 3:00 PM · Stop at a roadside venta for lunch en route
Stop 3 · Sep 24–27
Seville
3 Nights Luxurious Apartment · Historic District
Flamenco, Moorish palaces & the city that launched the New World
7Day
Arrival in Seville
Thursday, September 24, 2026
Afternoon
Arrive from Córdoba. Note that your apartment on Calle Hernando Colón (just steps from the Cathedral and Alcázar) checks in September 24 — arrange early luggage storage if arriving before 3:00 PM. Ask your host about early bag drop.
Late Afternoon
First wander through Santa Cruz — the ancient Jewish quarter turned most photogenic neighborhood in Spain. Tilework, orange trees, jasmine-scented alleys, and the great walls of the Alcázar looming overhead.
Evening
Plaza de España at dusk — the sweeping semicircular plaza built for the 1929 World’s Fair, with its tiled regional alcoves and canal boats. Then cross the river to Triana for your first Sevillano tapas: salmorejo, fried pescaíto, and Manzanilla.
8Day
Royal Alcázar & Cathedral
Friday, September 25, 2026
Morning
Real Alcázar — book the 9:00 AM slot. The finest surviving Mudéjar palace in the world, with extraordinary tiled rooms, carved stucco arches, and some of Spain’s most beautiful gardens. Game of Thrones fans will recognize the Water Gardens of Dorne. Allow 2+ hours.
Midday
Seville Cathedral — the world’s largest Gothic cathedral, and the tomb of Christopher Columbus. Climb the Giralda Tower (ramps, not stairs) for sweeping views over the rooftops.
Afternoon
Slow afternoon in Parque de María Luisa — shaded paths, fountains, peacocks, and the best people-watching in the city.
Evening
Dinner in Triana — cross the Puente de Isabel II into Seville's most soulful neighborhood. For a proper sit-down meal, try Restaurante El Faro de Triana on the riverfront for outstanding fresh fish and local wines, or Bar Santa Ana (one of Seville's oldest taverns) for classic tapas in an authentic neighborhood atmosphere. Dinner early — you have flamenco at 7:30 PM.
⚑ Tonight — 7:30 PM
Casa de la Memoria — one of the most intimate and celebrated flamenco venues in Seville, in a beautiful old palace courtyard on Calle Cuna. The show runs 7:30–8:30 PM. Seats are first-come, first-served — arrive by 7:00 PM for the best spots. A perfect Friday night in Seville.
💍

9Day
Move In & 🐂 Corrida de Toros
Saturday, September 26, 2026
Morning
Triana district in the morning — the neighborhood’s ceramic shops open early. Pick up hand-painted azulejo tiles as souvenirs. The Mercado de Triana is a great breakfast stop.
Afternoon
Check in to your apartment at Calle Hernando Colón, 10 at 3:00 PM — prime location in the historic district, steps from the Cathedral. Get settled; you have 3 nights here.
Afternoon / Optional
Metropol Parasol (Las Setas) — the futuristic wooden mushroom canopy over Plaza de la Encarnación. The rooftop walkway has excellent panoramic views of old Seville and is best in late afternoon light.
⚑ Evening — 6:30 PM Sharp
Tonight is the Corrida de Toros at the Plaza de Toros de la Real Maestranza — one of the oldest and most beautiful bullrings in Spain. Dress smartly; the atmosphere in the Sombra (shade) section is electric. Doors open well before the 6:30 PM start — arrive early to find your seats and soak in the pageantry. PDF tickets were sent to your email — print or save to your phone before leaving Oklahoma City.
🐂

Stop 4 · Sep 27–29
Ronda
2 Nights Las Vistas Residence
A hilltop city split by a gorge — and the oldest bullring in Spain
10Day
Arrival & The Gorge
Sunday, September 27, 2026
Afternoon
Arrive in Ronda. Check in to Las Vistas Residence on Calle Rosario — the name says it all. Drop your bags and walk directly to the Puente Nuevo (New Bridge) for your first look at the 100-meter El Tajo gorge. It will stop you cold.
Late Afternoon
Walk down to the Ciudad Vieja (old town on the far side of the bridge) — Arab baths, the Mondrágón Palace, and narrow streets that feel untouched. Ronda has almost no crowds compared to Seville or Granada.
Evening
Dinner with a gorge view. Several restaurants along the cliff edge have terraces overlooking the Tajo — reserve ahead. Ronda’s local wine (Serranía de Ronda DO) is excellent and underknown.
🏠
Las Vistas Residence — Best Views in Ronda
Calle Rosario, 14 Bajo Derecha · Ronda, Andalusia 29400 · Check-in 3:00 PM Sep 27 · Checkout 12:00 PM Sep 29
Confirmation: HMJ2WAF32T · Host: Daniel · +34 653 33 43 34
11Day
Bullring, Views & White Villages
Monday, September 28, 2026
Morning
Plaza de Toros de Ronda — the oldest bullring in Spain (1785), and the most beautiful. The museum inside traces the history of the corrida from its origins here. After last night’s bullfight in Seville, this gives you the full historical context.
Midday
Walk the Camino de los Molinos path below the gorge for the famous views back up at the Puente Nuevo from below. One of the great photographs in Spain. Bring your camera, Mark.
Afternoon / Optional
Day drive through the Pueblos Blancos (White Villages) — Grazalema, Zahara de la Sierra, or Setenil de las Bodegas (houses literally built into cliff overhangs). All within 30–45 minutes of Ronda.
Evening
Sundowners on a terrace with the last light hitting the gorge walls. Ronda at dusk is extraordinary. Farewell dinner — try local game dishes (venado, jabalí) from the surrounding mountains.
🚗
Travel · Tuesday, September 29, 2026 · ~1.75 hrs
Ronda → Nerja
Checkout by 12:00 PM · Scenic coastal drive via A-7 through Málaga · Arrive Costa del Sol · Check in Nerja from 1:00 PM
Stop 5 · Sep 29–30
Nerja
1 Night Hotel Carabeo
The Balcón de Europa — where the mountains meet the Mediterranean
12Day
Arrival, Coast & Caves
Tuesday, September 29, 2026
Afternoon
Check in to Hotel Carabeo — a charming boutique property on the clifftop street above the sea. Breakfast included. Pool open until 6:30 PM. The Balcón de Europa overlook is a 2-minute walk; it’s the defining image of Nerja, with views straight down to the Mediterranean and the Rif Mountains of Morocco visible on clear days.
Late Afternoon / Optional
Cuevas de Nerja (Nerja Caves) — a spectacular prehistoric cave system 3km east of town with cathedral-sized chambers and Paleolithic cave paintings. One of the best cave systems in Europe. Check closing times and book ahead.
Evening
Dinner at Restaurant 34 — Hotel Carabeo’s own restaurant with sea views. Hotel residents receive a 10% discount. Note: Restaurant is closed Mondays — Tuesday is perfect. Book a table when you check in. The freshest fish on the trip.

Granada
2 Nights Hotel Casa 1800
The Alhambra — the greatest Islamic palace in the Western world
13Day
Arrival & Albaicín at Dusk
Wednesday, September 30, 2026
Afternoon
Check in to Hotel Casa 1800 Granada on Calle Benalua — a beautifully restored 19th-century mansion steps from the Cathedral. Deluxe Premium Room, buffet breakfast included. This is the finest accommodation of the trip.
Late Afternoon
Walk up into the Albaicín quarter — the ancient Moorish hillside neighborhood with whitewashed lanes, Arabic tea houses, and sweeping views. Reach Mirador de San Nicolás before sunset for the iconic view of the Alhambra glowing against the Sierra Nevada. This single view may be the most beautiful thing you see in Spain.
Evening
Early dinner and early bed — your Alhambra private tour starts at 9:30 AM tomorrow. Granada’s famous tradition of a free tapa with every drink is active and generous; even a quick stop at a bar near the Cathedral will feed you well.

🏰 The Alhambra — Private Tour
Thursday, October 1, 2026
⚑ Early Start — Meet Your Guide at 9:30 AM
Buffet breakfast at Hotel Casa 1800 opens at 8:00 AM. Eat well — you’ll be on your feet for 3–4 hours. Taxi to the Alhambra (5 min) or walk up (20 min). Meet your private guide at 9:30 AM sharp at the Café Bar located next to the Ticket Office building at the Alhambra entrance.
Full Morning — Booked ✓
Alhambra & Generalife Complete Private Tour — your guide takes all four of you through the entire complex: the Nasrid Palaces (the jewel — intricate stucco, geometric tilework, the Court of the Lions), the Alcazaba fortress with its tower views, and the Generalife summer palace and garden terraces. With a private guide you’ll get context, stories, and access that most visitors miss entirely. This is the highlight of the trip.

📍 Notes for the Road

🚗
Driving in Spain
Speed limits: 120 km/h motorway, 90 rural, 50 town. Toll roads (autopistas) are fast but add up — carry a credit card. Parking in old city centers can be challenging; use paid lots. An International Driving Permit is recommended alongside your US license.
🌡️
Weather
Late September Andalucía: 24–30°C days, 16–18°C evenings. Seville can still be warm. Ronda and Granada are cooler due to elevation — bring a light layer for evenings. Nerja on the coast is mild and pleasant. This is the best time of year to visit.
🍽️
Eating in Spain
Lunch 2–4 PM, dinner 9–11 PM. The menú del día (lunch set menu, €12–18) is fantastic value. Granada’s free tapas with drinks are legendary — bar hop instead of sit-down dining for the authentic experience. Never rush a meal.
💶
Money
Euro (€). Budget roughly €80–120/person/day for meals, activities, and incidentals beyond accommodation. Credit cards are widely accepted, but carry €50–100 cash for small bars, markets, and tips. ATMs are abundant in city centers.
👜
Packing
Comfortable walking shoes are non-negotiable — cobblestones everywhere. Smart casual for evenings (especially the bullfight). Sunscreen and sunglasses essential. A small day bag for touring. Power adapter Type C/F for Spain.
🗣️
Language
Spanish (Castilian) throughout Andalucía. English is spoken in tourist areas and hotels. A few phrases go a long way: por favor (please), gracias (thank you), una mesa para cuatro (table for four), la cuenta (the bill). Locals appreciate any effort.
